History (AirGradient map's hourly history endpoint, 2026-09-28T14:00Z to 2026-09-30T07:00Z): 42/42 hourly buckets present, 100% uptime over its known life (first seen only ~42 h before capture, so long-term uptime is unverified). Last-24h mean 85.6 ug/m3 vs Larkin's (CA33J, API=162) implied 24-hr DOE PM2.5 of ~76.8 ug/m3 and Pasir Gudang's (CA34J, API=164) ~80.7 ug/m3 - within 6-11%, a real cross-check pass. Both Iolite and Eco Botanic show a steep, correlated drop in the last 1-2 h before capture (Iolite 89->20.6 ug/m3 hourly 01:00-07:00 UTC; Eco Botanic raw pm02 5.7 ug/m3 at 08:08 UTC vs a corrected pm25 of 1.7), consistent with a real local rain/clearing event, not a fault, since both independent sensors moved together. BLOCKER: HazeNow's own agMapObservations() (packages/core/src/countries/sources/airgradient.ts) filters `r.dataSource !== 'AirGradient'` and drops every Sensor.Community row from the map API response, so Iolite is visible in the raw upstream payload but not ingested by the current adapter code. This is an engineering gap (a filter to relax or a second adapter branch for Sensor.Community), not a permissions problem - Sensor.Community is ODbL, CORS *, no key.
verdict: coverable via proxy once the adapter reads Sensor.Community rows too (small code change, no external permission needed); today's live picture is unchanged (24-hr DOE index only, no now number)

notes: MAJOR FINDING for Sarawak's worst-haze city: met.gov.my/pencerapan/zarah-terampai-teom-pm-10 (discovered from the official nav menu, 'Sains Atmosfera > Zarah Terampai (TEOM PM-10/PM-2.5)') links to 7 PDFs, one per weekday name (Isnin..Ahad), each an hourly PM2.5 bar chart 'Kepekatan Purata Setiap Jam Zarah Terampai Bagi Bandar-Bandar Utama di Malaysia' for exactly 4 TEOM stations nationwide: Cameron Highlands, Kuching, Petaling Jaya and Lembah Danum (Sabah). This is a SEPARATE agency and a SEPARATE, genuinely-hourly PM2.5 measurement (TEOM = Tapered Element Oscillating Microbalance), independent of DOE's 24-hr API index. Fetched all 7 PDFs live today (2026-09-30): all last-modified simultaneously at 2026-09-29T16:32 UTC (a weekly batch refresh), and the 'Rabu'/'Khamis' (Wed/Thu) files show data dated 23/24 September 2026 - i.e. last week's Wed/Thu, confirming a ~6-7 day publish lag, not a live feed. Every sampled file (Rabu, Khamis checked in full) carries the same note: Kuching's own TEOM station has been down 'due to a technical fault, until further notice.' So even the stale archive has nothing for Kuching right now. DOE APIMS Kuching (CA65Q) today: API=58 'Moderate' at 16:00 MYT (much calmer than the 28 Sep episode where IPD Serian hit 158; all 13 Sarawak stations read Good/Moderate today). AirGradient/Sensor.Community: still 0 sensors within 25 km of Kuching, re-confirmed today.
verdict: authoritative permission is the only way for a true 1-hr number here - email Jabatan Meteorologi Malaysia (met.gov.my) to ask for (1) real-time/API access to the Kuching TEOM feed instead of the weekly PDF, and (2) the status of the technical fault. Until then, coverage stays exactly as today: DOE's 24-hr index only (needs_proxy, unchanged).

source: NEW candidate: MET Malaysia (Jabatan Meteorologi Malaysia) TEOM PM2.5 station, Cameron Highlands - genuinely hourly, right at the destination, but not accessible live today

notes: This is the most consequential finding for Malaysia: Cameron Highlands is currently 'not_feasible' in places.ts with the stated reason 'the nearest DOE station is 34 km away and 1,400 m lower, so it can't stand for the highlands' - but MET Malaysia runs an actual TEOM PM2.5 instrument in Cameron Highlands itself (one of only 4 in the country: Cameron Highlands, Kuching, Petaling Jaya, Lembah Danum). Found via met.gov.my's own navigation ('Pencerapan > Sains Atmosfera > Zarah Terampai (TEOM PM-10/PM-2.5)') -> 7 PDFs (https://www.met.gov.my/data/bsapa/PM2.5-<Weekday>.pdf), one slot per weekday name, refreshed as a batch (all 7 files last-modified 2026-09-29T16:32 UTC). Today's 'Khamis' (Thursday) file, fetched live, shows a Cameron Highland chart dated 24 September 2026 with hourly bars ~0.4-6.9 ug/m3 (a 3-hour rolling average overlay) - very clean air, plausible for a highland tea-plantation town, but 6 days stale and with no per-bar numeric labels to extract precisely (the Petaling Jaya panel on the same PDF does print 'Max: NN.NN' per hour, so the underlying data clearly has per-hour numbers - MET's chart generator just doesn't always render the label). No AirGradient/Sensor.Community sensor within a tight Tanah Rata/Brinchang bbox today (0 rows) - unchanged.
verdict: authoritative permission is the only way - email Jabatan Meteorologi Malaysia (met.gov.my) to ask for (1) real-time/API access to the Cameron Highlands TEOM feed instead of the weekly PDF, and (2) numeric (not just chart) hourly values. This would be a genuine official-1h source, a first for Malaysia outside the DOE system. Until then, Cameron Highlands should move from 'not feasible' to 'needs permission' in the app's own language, since the honest story is now 'the data exists, we know who to ask' rather than 'nothing exists here.'
